instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, grate 6 oz of the havarti and 6 oz of the Colby Jack on the large holes of a box grater. That's about 2 cups of each.

Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium. Add the 1/3 cup panko with a pinch of salt and the pinch of pepper, and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until the crumbs are golden brown and smell toasty.
Take the skillet off the heat, stir in the 2 tbsp Parmesan and tip the crumbs into a small bowl.
When the water boils, add the 12 oz macaroni and cook it until it's al dente, about 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
While the pasta cooks, whisk the can of evaporated milk, the 2 eggs and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt together in a medium saucepan until no streaks of egg are left. Add both grated cheeses.

Set the saucepan over medium low and whisk constantly for 6 to 8 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat the whisk. Take it off the heat as soon as it thickens. Don't let it boil, or the eggs will curdle.
Scoop out about 3/4 cup of the pasta water and set it aside. Drain the macaroni and put it back in its pot.

Whisk the 1/3 cup sour cream into the cheese sauce, then pour the sauce over the macaroni and stir until every piece is coated. If it's thicker than you like, stir in a splash of the pasta water at a time until it loosens.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve right away, with the toasted crumbs scattered over the top.
method_notes: Natasha's Kitchen leads with a stovetop sauce of evaporated milk, eggs, havarti and Colby Jack whisked over medium low until it just thickens, finished off the heat with sour cream and loosened with pasta water. Whisk It Real Good makes a butter and flour roux with milk, cheddar and Parmesan instead, and America's Test Kitchen cooks the pasta right in milk and water and melts American cheese and cheddar into it, then tops it with panko toasted in oil and tossed with Parmesan. This follows Natasha's sauce, which serves 8 as a side, at full size for 4 dinner bowls, and borrows the toasted crumb topping from America's Test Kitchen for crunch. Fine sea salt in the lead swaps one for one with table salt.
